argument_summary: The supportable position is not a clean pass with minor caveats. Certification is defensible only as disclosed certification: aggregate performance clears the deployment threshold, but the small-business support slice remains an unresolved material weakness that must be stated in the audit packet. The smaller sample and wider confidence interval justify rechecking the slice in the next eval batch, but they do not remove the present disclosure obligation or convert this into clean certification.
claims_about_policy: The admissible record supports a narrow policy claim: aggregate pass rates can support launch readiness, but they do not erase subgroup weaknesses. Under the policy text and BMCARD-030-C, a weakness that may materially affect a protected or contractual customer segment must be disclosed unless an approved mitigation removes exposure. BMCARD-030-E shows there is no approved mitigation in the record. BMCARD-030-D supports follow-up confirmation because of sampling uncertainty, but policy expressly does not allow that uncertainty to transform an unresolved materiality issue into a clean certification basis.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost claim changes compliance status. The risk-weighted point is narrower: where aggregate performance is above threshold, disclosed certification avoids turning slice uncertainty into a deployment block while still preserving the required warning to downstream reviewers and customers. That supports limiting escalation so long as certification is explicitly caveated rather than presented as a clean pass.
concessions: The small-business support slice is below both its warning and preferred thresholds.
There is no approved mitigation in the admissible record.
Sampling uncertainty reduces confidence in the slice estimate but does not eliminate the weakness.
Certification should not be defended as 'minor caveats' or as a clean pass.
